routes.label: Count cycles in the dual graph

question: Each of the \(12\) edges of a cube is labeled \(0\) or \(1.\) Two labelings are considered different even if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of one or more rotations and/or reflections. For how many such labelings is the sum of the labels on the edges of each of the \(6\) faces of the cube equal to \(2?\)
solution:
Use the four vertical edges to organize the count. Label the bottom vertices \(1,2,3,4\) cyclically, as shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q24_solution_fig1.svg)

Let \(b_i\) label the bottom edge from vertex \(i\) to the next vertex, let \(v_i\) label the vertical edge above \(i\), and let \(t_i\) label the top edge above \(b_i\). Subscripts wrap around, so \(v_5=v_1\).

Each side face must have sum \(2\), which forces
\[
t_i=2-b_i-v_i-v_{i+1}.
\]
The bottom face has \(\sum b_i=2\). Adding the four equations shows that the top sum is \(8-2-2\sum v_i\). Since the top sum is also \(2\), we must have \(\sum v_i=2\). Exactly two of the four vertical labels are therefore \(1\).

If those two \(1\)'s are opposite, there are \(2\) choices of their positions. Every consecutive pair of vertical labels then has sum \(1\), so \(t_i=1-b_i\). Any choice of two \(1\)'s on the bottom works, giving \(\binom42=6\) choices and \(2\cdot6=12\) labelings.

If the two vertical \(1\)'s are adjacent, there are \(4\) choices of their positions. The bottom edge between them must be \(0\), since otherwise its forced top label would be \(-1\). The opposite bottom edge, between the two vertical \(0\)'s, must be \(1\), since otherwise its forced top label would be \(2\). The other two bottom edges must contain one \(1\) and one \(0\), giving \(2\) choices and \(4\cdot2=8\) labelings.

In each case the top labels are uniquely forced, are \(0\) or \(1\), and have sum \(2\). Thus every counted labeling is valid. Rotated labelings count separately as requested, so the total is \(12+8=\boxed{20}\), choice E.
